# LALUM

> LALUM is a Tech-Legal practice uniting law, real estate, and artificial intelligence, led by Dr. Avraham Lalum (Attorney and Notary, Ph.D. in Law and Economics). Based in Herzliya, Israel, LALUM guides property deals and buyers in Israel and abroad, represents owners and rights-holders, runs decision-oriented mediation (DOM), and governs AI risk with EU AI Act conformity.

LALUM brings law, real estate, and AI together in one practice. On the real estate side it guides buyers and investors through transactions in Israel and abroad, represents owners and rights-holders, and handles urban renewal. On the AI side it turns legal risk into a system that can be controlled: certified, ex-ante legal opinions, documented conformity, and defensible records. This site provides general information and is not legal advice; an attorney and client relationship begins only with a signed engagement.

## What LALUM does

- Representing overseas property buyers: guiding buyers and investors through property deals in Israel and abroad, from due diligence to closing.
- Representation of property owners and rights-holders: protecting owners, sellers, and holders of rights in real estate matters and disputes.
- Real estate transactions and urban renewal: purchase, sale, and urban renewal deals, with the tax and contract layer handled end to end.
- Mediation and Dispute Resolution (DOM): Decision-Oriented Mediation for real estate, corporate, AI, and regulatory disputes.
- AI Regulation and EU AI Act conformity: risk classification, GPAI obligations, technical documentation, and a conformity matrix for technology exporters and for M&A and VC due diligence.
- AI Liability and Risk Governance: a conformity index and executive exposure matrix for boards, executives, and CPAs.
- IP and Data Protection: a defensible IP layer and a secure, Privacy-by-Design data architecture.
- Contracts and Venture Counsel: contract governance, counsel for startups and technology companies, funding rounds, founder agreements, and technology due diligence.
- Public Sector AI: explainable, bias-audited decision systems for authorities, ministries, and public tenders.

## Languages

The site is available in Hebrew (primary), English, Spanish, French, and Arabic. Every page renders in all five; the non-Hebrew rendering of any page is reachable by adding ?lang=en, ?lang=es, ?lang=fr, or ?lang=ar to its address.

Ramat Gan Municipality, 22.3.2026), the Privacy Protection Authority's clarification barring LPR cameras for parking enforcement, the public-body duties under Privacy Protection Amendment 13, and two working tools: a human-oversight protocol and a CEO readiness checklist.

## Featured articles

- The EU AI Act is here, what Israeli leadership must do now: https://lalumapp.com/insights/eu-ai-act-2026/ . The AI Act already applies; how boards and Israeli companies operating in Europe should map exposure, classify systems (prohibited, transparency, GPAI, high-risk), anchor human accountability, and keep a defensible evidence file.
- The black box fallacy, why unexplainable AI is a legal liability: https://lalumapp.com/insights/explainability/ . Accuracy without the ability to reason is exposure; the governance controls a board must be able to evidence on demand.
- The corporate trap, are your AI models leaking the organization's IP: https://lalumapp.com/insights/sovereignty/ . Feeding confidential contracts and client records into third-party models as a privacy and trade-secret breach, and zero-data-leakage architecture.
- Board liability for algorithmic decisions: https://lalumapp.com/insights/board-liability/ . When automated decisions expose directors and officers personally, and the record that defends them.
- Public sector AI and procurement: https://lalumapp.com/insights/procurement/ . Explainable, bias-audited decision systems that withstand administrative petitions and State Comptroller review.
- AI in banking and finance, regulation and legal risk: https://lalumapp.com/insights/ai-banking-finance-regulation-risk/ . Where AI sits across banking and finance (credit, fraud, AML, insurance pricing, advice), the legal risk of each (discrimination in credit, explainability to the customer, EU AI Act high-risk classification, board accountability, vendor risk), and how to build governance that holds before a regulator and a customer.
- Lawyers using AI, accountability and ethics: https://lalumapp.com/insights/lawyers-ai-ethics-accountability/ . The normative regime for a lawyer's use of AI: when a tool crosses into unauthorized practice of law (section 20, the discretion/harm/access test), what Israeli and foreign courts ruled on relying on fabricated AI citations (Mata v. Avianca, and the verified Israeli rulings), and what the bar's ethics guidance permits and forbids on confidentiality, informed written consent and human supervision.
- Developer agreement in urban renewal, the critical clauses: https://lalumapp.com/insights/developer-agreement-urban-renewal-critical-clauses/ . Six clauses that decide a homeowner deal: apartment area and specification, binding milestones with late-delivery compensation, guarantees written into the contract, rent during evacuation, developer substitution, and plan changes.
- AI in insurance, underwriting, pricing and claims under regulatory supervision: https://lalumapp.com/insights/ai-insurance-underwriting-pricing-regulation/ . Bias in underwriting, fairness versus accuracy in pricing, human review of flagged claims, vendor contract protections, and a governance framework.
- A real estate contract drafted with AI, what to check before signing: https://lalumapp.com/insights/ai-drafted-real-estate-contract-review/ . Why an AI drafted property or urban renewal contract can read correct yet omit protections (guarantees, caution note, staged payments, conditions), the fabricated legal reference risk, a practical pre signing checklist, and why responsibility stays with the signer.
- AI in a local authority, four uses and the legal limit of each: https://lalumapp.com/insights/ai-local-authorities-uses-legal-limits/ . Resident chatbots, algorithmic enforcement, licensing and planning, and internal decisions, where each one crosses a legal line for a public authority, anchored to the verified Israeli ruling on a municipality that relied on AI without control.
- AI in municipal licensing and planning, how far statutory discretion reaches: https://lalumapp.com/insights/ai-planning-permits-local-authority-discretion/ . Where AI enters permit triage and planning files, why the local committee's statutory discretion cannot be delegated to a model, the permitted line between assistance and decision, the duty to give reasons, and the double exposure of administrative challenge and downstream urban renewal disputes.
- Algorithm-based municipal enforcement, when it is lawful and what due process requires: https://lalumapp.com/insights/ai-municipal-algorithmic-enforcement-due-process/ . Cameras, sensors and systems that flag violations, why flagging is not adjudication, the due-process trio of notice, right to be heard and a reasoned decision, meaningful human review versus a rubber stamp, the evidentiary burden in the concrete case, and the ban on biased or selective enforcement, anchored to the verified Israeli ruling.
- AI use policy for a local authority, what the administrative-law layer adds beyond a private policy: https://lalumapp.com/insights/ai-use-policy-local-authority/ . Why a municipality cannot copy a private company's AI policy, mapping uses by impact, what the written policy must contain (human control, assist-versus-decide line, duty to give reasons, bias checks, resident-data privacy, audit trail, accountability), and the procurement clauses to require from a vendor, anchored to the verified Israeli ruling.
- AI procurement and tenders for a local authority, what to require from the vendor: https://lalumapp.com/insights/ai-procurement-tender-local-authority/ . Why the tender is the moment of leverage, the contract clauses a municipality must secure (audit right, transparency of method and limits, data location and non-training and deletion, cooperation in legal proceedings, liability and indemnity, exit and no vendor lock-in), the public-procurement-law layer (no tailored tenders, reasoned winner choice, AI-specific scoring criteria), and why administrative liability never transfers to the vendor.
- Privacy and resident data when a local authority runs AI: https://lalumapp.com/insights/ai-resident-data-privacy-local-authority/ . Why resident data is different (given under state compulsion for a defined purpose), the legal basis needed to process it through an AI tool, the data-minimization and anonymization duty, resident transparency and access rights, the higher bar for sensitive data and vulnerable groups, and why the authority stays the controller when a vendor or cloud does the processing.
- Municipal chatbot and automated resident responses, the authority's legal exposure: https://lalumapp.com/insights/ai-municipal-chatbot-resident-liability/ . Why a wrong answer a resident relied on is the authority's exposure, the line between general information and a binding representation, scoping topics the bot answers versus those it escalates, the accessibility duties (languages and disability) that bind a public body, the required path to a binding human answer, and privacy in the chat, anchored to the verified Israeli ruling.
- The required majority in urban renewal and the holdout owner: https://lalumapp.com/insights/urban-renewal-required-majority-holdout/ . How the law replaced unanimity with a qualified majority (which differs by track and has been amended, so the exact figure must be checked), the holdout-owner mechanism under the pinui-binui law (a damages claim before the land-registration supervisor, and in defined cases a functionary who signs in the owner's stead), and the grounds that make a refusal reasonable and protect the individual owner.
- Taxation in urban renewal for the apartment owner: https://lalumapp.com/insights/urban-renewal-taxation-owner/ . The three taxes an owner meets (betterment levy, land-appreciation tax, purchase tax), why the law builds targeted reliefs so the renewal itself is not taxed, and where exposure arises (consideration beyond the relief cap, upgrades, wrong deal structure, assuming an exemption applies automatically). Conceptual, pointing to the current statute for exact rates and caps.
- Consideration in pinui-binui, how to read and value a developer's offer: https://lalumapp.com/insights/pinui-binui-consideration-valuation/ . Why the headline is not the deal, how to compute the net consideration after costs, why the binding spec of the new apartment and the guarantees matter more than added square meters, independent owners'-side appraisal versus marketing figures, and comparing offers on a common basis.
- The owners' representation in urban renewal, role, powers and limits: https://lalumapp.com/insights/urban-renewal-owners-representation/ . What the representation does (coordinates owners, selects and instructs the owners'-side professionals, negotiates with the developer), what it cannot do (it is not a substitute for each owner's individual consent), where its authority comes from (a clear written mandate), and the quiet danger of conflicts of interest and professionals who are not truly independent of the developer.
- AI in international transactions, where it accelerates and where the legal risk is: https://lalumapp.com/insights/ai-international-transactions-overview/ . How AI speeds cross-border deals (summarizing foreign documents, bridging language, first-pass due diligence, counterparty and sanctions screening), where exposure concentrates (translation shifting legal meaning, foreign-law assumptions, verification of foreign registries, compliance), the rule that the tool accelerates while a qualified human who knows the relevant jurisdictions decides and verifies, and why crossing borders multiplies every risk. The intersection of the firm's two focus areas.
- Principles agreement versus detailed agreement in urban renewal, what already binds: https://lalumapp.com/insights/urban-renewal-principles-vs-detailed-agreement/ . Why the binding force is set by content and conduct, not by the label "principles"; what a principles agreement or MOU can already commit (exclusivity, locked core terms, reliance); why the real deal lives in the detailed agreement; what to keep open (milestone-bound and time-limited exclusivity, an exit); and why counsel is needed before signing the principles, not only for the detailed agreement.
- Pinui-binui, a full owner guide: https://lalumapp.com/insights/pinui-binui-owner-guide/ . What owners need through an evacuate-and-rebuild urban renewal project: how it differs from TAMA 38, the stages, the required majority and the holdout owner, the guarantees (sale-law, rent, defects, registration), taxation, and independent legal representation.
- TAMA 38/1 versus TAMA 38/2: https://lalumapp.com/insights/tama-38-1-vs-38-2-comparison/ . The difference between strengthening-and-adding (38/1) and demolition-and-rebuild (38/2), the practical trade-offs, feasibility, owner guarantees, and how to choose the right track for a building.
- Israel's real-estate brokerage reform, a professional guide: https://lalumapp.com/insights/מדריך-מקצועי-למתווכים-רפורמת-התיווך-במקרקעין-של-משרד-המשפטים/ . The Ministry of Justice's real-estate brokerage reform: the professional and transparency principles, fairness toward both sides of a deal, and what changed in practice for brokers and their clients.
- Portugal real estate, Porto versus Lisbon for the Israeli investor: https://lalumapp.com/insights/portugal-porto-vs-lisbon/ . Comparing the two cities for an Israeli property investor, yield versus risk, the planning and rental-use considerations to check, and the value of an independent legal opinion and Legal-AI-assisted due diligence before choosing.
- Portugal real estate taxation for an Israeli resident: https://lalumapp.com/insights/portugal-real-estate-taxation/ . Local Portuguese purchase and holding taxes, taxation of rental income and capital gains, the Israel-Portugal tax treaty against double taxation, and the Israeli reporting duty on worldwide income.
- Legal due diligence on a Portuguese property, and how Legal AI speeds it: https://lalumapp.com/insights/portugal-legal-due-diligence/ . Verifying title and registration where there is no Israeli-style Tabu, property documents, liens and building irregularities, and how Legal AI tools accelerate reviewing foreign-language documents under a lawyer's supervision.
- Obligations by role under the EU AI Act, provider, deployer, distributor, importer: https://lalumapp.com/insights/eu-ai-act-roles-obligations/ . How the EU AI Act splits duties by role in the supply chain: the provider's heavy package, the deployer's use and human-oversight duties, the gatekeeping duties of importer and distributor, when a deployer becomes a provider through substantial modification or rebranding, and how an Israeli company maps its role before building a compliance plan.
- AI product liability, the revised EU Product Liability Directive: https://lalumapp.com/insights/ai-product-liability-eu/ . How the revised EU product-liability regime brings software and AI systems within product liability, eases the claimant's burden of proof through evidence disclosure and presumptions, who is exposed (including importers when the maker is outside the EU), how it complements the EU AI Act, and what an Israeli company selling an AI product into Europe should do.
- AI regulation in Israel, the approach, what already applies, and what is expected: https://lalumapp.com/insights/israel-ai-regulation-policy/ . Israel's principles-based, sectoral approach rather than one comprehensive AI law, what already binds through existing law (privacy and Amendment 13, anti-discrimination, consumer protection, tort, IP), the practical pull of the EU AI Act on Israeli companies, the likely direction, and why to build AI governance now rather than wait for a statute.
- Case study, IP value collapse in an acquisition from AI code leakage: https://lalumapp.com/insights/ip-value-collapse-ai-acquisition/ . An anonymized composite scenario where a tech company's proprietary code and data leaked to an AI vendor's training set through unmanaged AI agents, so due diligence found the loss of IP exclusivity irreversible, cutting deal value sharply and unwinding founder earn-out incentives, and the governance, tool-choice and contractual layers that would have prevented it.
- Compliance for Israeli SaaS companies selling to the EU: https://lalumapp.com/insights/saas-eu-compliance-israeli-companies/ . The compliance map for an Israeli SaaS vendor selling into Europe: when EU law applies, GDPR duties, cross-border data-transfer mechanisms, data processing agreements with customers and sub-processors, the intersection with the EU AI Act, and building a compliance map before due diligence forces it.
- Amendment 13, when a DPO appointment is mandatory: https://lalumapp.com/insights/amendment-13-dpo-appointment/ . Who must appoint a Data Protection Officer under Israel's Privacy Protection Amendment 13, the DPO's role and powers, the independence and organizational-placement requirement, in-house versus external DPO, the consequences of failing to appoint, and practical steps.
- Attorney-client privilege in the AI era: https://lalumapp.com/insights/attorney-client-privilege-ai/ . What happens to attorney-client privilege and professional confidentiality when a lawyer feeds client material into an AI tool: the waiver risk, the decisive distinction between a tool that trains on the data and one contractually bound not to, professional-ethics duties, and practical steps for a firm to adopt AI without breaking privilege.
- Partnership dissolution in the AI era, who owns the firm's AI agents: https://lalumapp.com/insights/partnership-dissolution-ai-ownership/ . When a professional partnership dissolves, who gets the fine-tuned AI agents trained on the firm's files and know-how: the new asset partnership agreements ignore, the indivisibility of a trained model and its data, the licensing illusion, the client-confidentiality dimension, and why the fix is a dedicated AI annex to the partnership agreement.
- Amendment 13 data security guide: https://lalumapp.com/insights/amendment-13-data-security-guide/ . The data-security obligations under Israel's Privacy Protection Amendment 13: security levels by database sensitivity, technical and organizational controls, written procedures, access management, incident handling and reporting, audits, and staff training.

## Training programs

Six sessions of three hours each, 24 academic hours, with a practical capstone. Taught by Dr. Avraham Lalum, attorney, notary and Ph.D. in Law and Economics. The In-House line is delivered at the client's offices for organisations; the Academy Pro line is online, for individual professionals, and awards a participation certificate.

- LALUM Academy: AI בעסקאות נדל״ן מורכבות והתחדשות עירונית: https://lalumapp.com/training/lalum-academy-real-estate/ . נדל״ן והתחדשות עירונית. מחלקות משפטיות, חברות יזמיות, משרדי עורכי דין ומנהלי פרויקטים בנדל״ן.
- LALUM Academy: חוזים מורכבים, ממשל תאגידי ואוטומציה: https://lalumapp.com/training/lalum-academy-corporate/ . ממשל תאגידי וחוזים. יועצים משפטיים פנימיים (In-House), מנהלי סיכונים, קציני ציות (Compliance) ומנהלי עסקאות.
- LALUM Academy: ליטיגציה, ראיות דיגיטליות, גישור ובוררות: https://lalumapp.com/training/lalum-academy-litigation/ . ליטיגציה ויישוב סכסוכים. ליטיגטורים, מנהלי מחלקות סכסוכים, בוררים, מגשרים ומנהלי סיכונים משפטיים.
- LALUM Academy: AI Legal & Regulatory Engineering for Hi-Tech: https://lalumapp.com/training/lalum-academy-hitech/ . הייטק והנדסה רגולטורית. יועצים משפטיים בהייטק (GC), מנהלי מוצר (VP Product/CPO), סמנכ״לי טכנולוגיה (CTO) ומנהלי R&D.
- LALUM Academy: AI לרשויות מקומיות ולמגזר הציבורי: https://lalumapp.com/training/lalum-academy-public-sector/ . רשויות מקומיות וגופים ציבוריים. מנהלי מחלקות ברשויות מקומיות, לשכות משפטיות ציבוריות, מבקרי פנים, ממוני חופש מידע וצוותי רגולציה.
- LALUM Academy: AI המשפטי לתעשיית הרכב והניידות: https://lalumapp.com/training/lalum-academy-automotive/ . תעשיית הרכב וניידות. יועצים משפטיים ומנהלי רגולציה ביבואני ויצרני רכב, חברות ניידות, ביטוח רכב וניהול צי.
- LALUM Academy: AI המשפטי לבריאות ולמדעי החיים: https://lalumapp.com/training/lalum-academy-healthcare/ . בריאות ומדעי החיים. יועצים משפטיים בקופות חולים, בתי חולים, חברות מכשור רפואי, פארמה ובריאות דיגיטלית.
- LALUM Academy: AI המשפטי לפיננסים ולביטוח: https://lalumapp.com/training/lalum-academy-finance/ . פיננסים וביטוח. יועצים משפטיים וקציני ציות בבנקים, חברות ביטוח, בתי השקעות, פינטק וגופים מוסדיים.
- LALUM Academy: AI המשפטי לאנרגיה, תשתיות ותעשייה: https://lalumapp.com/training/lalum-academy-energy/ . אנרגיה, תשתיות ותעשייה. יועצים משפטיים ומנהלי רגולציה בחברות אנרגיה, תשתיות, בנייה ותעשייה יצרנית.
- LALUM Academy: AI המשפטי לסייבר והגנת מידע: https://lalumapp.com/training/lalum-academy-cyber/ . סייבר והגנת מידע. יועצים משפטיים, מנהלי אבטחת מידע (CISO), ממוני הגנת פרטיות (DPO) וצוותי ציות וניהול סיכונים.
- LALUM Academy Pro: AI לעורך הדין העצמאי ולמשרד הבוטיק: https://lalumapp.com/training/lalum-academy-pro-law/ . עורכי דין. עורכי דין עצמאיים ומשרדי בוטיק שרוצים להטמיע כלי AI בעבודה היומיומית בלי לפגוע בחיסיון ובאחריות המקצועית.
- LALUM Academy Pro: AI לשמאי המקרקעין: https://lalumapp.com/training/lalum-academy-pro-appraisal/ . שמאי מקרקעין. שמאי מקרקעין עצמאיים ומשרדי שמאות שרוצים לקצר את שלב איסוף הנתונים והניתוח בלי לפגוע באחריות המקצועית על השומה.
- LALUM Academy Pro: AI לרואה החשבון וליועץ המס: https://lalumapp.com/training/lalum-academy-pro-accounting/ . רואי חשבון ויועצי מס. רואי חשבון, יועצי מס ומנהלי חשבונות בכירים שרוצים לקצר סיווג, הצלבה ואיתור חריגים בלי לוותר על בקרה.
